nodes.summary: A class of finite groups is a predicate on finite groups: it assigns to every finite group $G$ a proposition, read as "$G$ belongs to the class". The class need not be closed under isomorphism.
nodes.title: Classes of finite groups

nodes.summary: There is a finite group $G$ such that infinitely many formations are contained in the formation generated by $G$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 16.31 is negative, even for finite $G$.
nodes.title: The formation generated by a finite group can have infinitely many subformations

nodes.summary: The statement (V. A. Vedernikov) that for every finite group $G$ only finitely many formations of finite groups are contained in the formation generated by $G$. Here formations may be empty, and a formation $\mathfrak{F}$ is contained in the formation generated by $G$ when every finite group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to the formation generated by $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.31 for finite groups

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$, the formation generated by $G$ is the class of finite groups $H$ such that $H$ belongs to every formation that contains $G$; that is, it is the intersection of all formations containing $G$.
nodes.title: Formation generated by a finite group

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups is a formation if it is closed under homomorphic images (whenever $f \colon G \to H$ is a surjective homomorphism of finite groups and $G \in \mathfrak{F}$, then $H \in \mathfrak{F}$) and under finite subdirect products (whenever $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of a finite group $G$ with $G / N_1 \in \mathfrak{F}$ and $G / N_2 \in \mathfrak{F}$, then…
nodes.title: Formations of finite groups, possibly empty
